source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Use a wrong user account to log in web UI
2. Use correct admin accounts  to log in web UI
3. Log out from web UI

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Should NOT log in with wrong user account
2. Should be logged in with correct admin accounts of different privileges successfully
3. Should be back to login page after logout

original_test_intent: The title appears to require a BMC web login path meaningfully based on or associated with a MAC address, while the preserved Procedure and Criteria define only ordinary wrong-account, admin-account and logout checks and never identify how MAC participates or what unique result proves it.
original_method: Unresolved. The body describes a standard BMC web login/logout matrix, but the title may refer to a vendor MAC-derived hostname, discovery service, local link-layer access, certificate/device identity check, credential/account relation or copied/mislabeled content; the Master does not choose among them.
manual_activity: An engineer must decide what `Login with MAC` means and map the title to an explicit supported access mechanism and acceptance checkpoint, or declare the body to be the intended generic login test. Only after that decision may an agent prepare a browser/account workflow; no MAC-based mechanism may be invented by the reviewer.
required_inputs: Authoritative statement of whether `MAC` is a BMC interface identifier, MAC-derived hostname, discovery key, URL/address token, access-control credential, certificate/device-binding input or erroneous title

If MAC-based access is intended: exact target interface/MAC, canonical formatting, VLAN/broadcast/domain scope, discovery/resolution protocol and server, browser URL/authority syntax, IPv4/IPv6 result and cache lifetime
Unique acceptance criterion proving the chosen MAC mechanism was used rather than ordinary IP/FQDN access, including negative/wrong-MAC behavior if required
If generic login is intended: approved correction/override explaining why the MAC title is not covered and how this row differs from ordinary and domain-name login cases
After scope resolution: immutable BMC/certificate/firmware identity, protected disposable account/privilege matrix, bounded invalid attempt, session invalidation, audit evidence and recovery
safety_requirements: Do not convert a raw MAC address into an IP address, hostname or URL by guesswork. No standard/vendor mapping is supplied in this row, and a plausible derived endpoint may identify another device.

Do not follow DeepSeek/GPT V2's hypothetical MAC-resolution route until the Project/vendor explicitly defines it; DNS, mDNS, hosts overrides and vendor discovery are different mechanisms with different coverage.
Do not run the generic login/logout body and claim `Login with MAC` passed. That would omit the only title-specific purpose.

Do not authenticate to any discovered/resolved endpoint until its BMC identity, interface MAC, certificate, firmware and Project ownership are independently bound; wrong-target authentication can disclose admin credentials.

After scope resolution, use protected disposable accounts and cap invalid attempts below lockout/alarm thresholds; preserve security logs and verify logout by session invalidation, not redirect alone.
Do not clear dmesg, syslog, SEL or BMC audit logs. Do not automatically retry discovery or authentication on ambiguous/stale/multiple results.
Stop if the engineer cannot define a unique MAC checkpoint, if the selected mechanism is unsupported by the platform, or if endpoint identity/recovery cannot be proven.
agent_execution_scope: Before the engineer decision, preserve the source and collect only non-mutating documentation evidence about candidate platform mechanisms; do not resolve invented names, edit hosts/DNS, browse a derived endpoint or submit credentials.

After an approved scope, verify the exact MAC/interface and chosen mechanism end-to-end, bind its resolution/access result to BMC certificate/firmware identity and record the unique MAC-specific checkpoint.
Only then execute the approved bounded wrong-account, correct-role and logout/session-invalidation matrix with protected accounts and preserved audit evidence.
Report any unverified source branch or Project Override coverage explicitly; never issue DUT PASS/FAIL or retry automatically.
engineer_actions: Resolve the title/body conflict by defining `MAC`, its role in the login path, the supported mechanism and unique expected result, or approve a generic-login interpretation with recorded uncovered title coverage.
Approve the exact BMC/interface/network scope, endpoint identity binding, account matrix, attempt limits, recovery and any configuration/setup required by the chosen mechanism.
Review the MAC-specific and authentication/session evidence independently and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It is not valid as a final method because `hostname/mac-based URL` is not present in the Master and represents multiple non-equivalent vendor/network mechanisms. A page/login result cannot prove how the endpoint was derived, and the generic body does not supply a MAC checkpoint.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No execution command or URL should be recommended until an engineer defines the authoritative MAC mechanism and acceptance signal. Afterward, use the platform-supported discovery/access procedure and a separately bounded browser login/logout matrix with exact identity evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The `Login with MAC` title, generic wrong/admin/logout body, absence of Script and 5/0-minute estimates remain preserved as conflicting source facts.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: First align the title with one documented platform mechanism and define its unique evidence; then test endpoint identity plus the three authentication/session checkpoints without allowing generic login to substitute for MAC coverage.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the BMC firmware/network architecture that explicitly supports the engineer-selected MAC-based mechanism.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware, interface inventory, discovery/resolution service and browser versions after scope resolution.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project/vendor documentation for the chosen MAC mechanism, BMC web endpoint identity and account/session behavior.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Does not invent a missing MAC method; it makes the unresolved title-specific coverage an explicit decision before executing the generic body.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Ordinary IP or domain login proves authentication only; address-resolution success proves discovery only; neither proves an undefined `Login with MAC` objective. Each uncovered dimension must remain recorded.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Engineer scope decision, mechanism, identity map, unique acceptance, accounts, security and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A guessed mapping can send credentials to the wrong device; cache/proxy/discovery ambiguity can create false evidence; generic login can mask the absent MAC function.

project_override_considerations: A Project may define a MAC-derived hostname/discovery service or decide that the title is erroneous, but must record preserved title/body, actual mechanism, reason, engineer approval, unique evidence and any original MAC coverage left unverified. The next Domain Name case cannot automatically be reused as this case's meaning.
expected_evidence: Signed engineer decision defining `Login with MAC`, the selected platform mechanism and unique acceptance criteria
Exact target BMC/interface MAC, network scope and authoritative vendor/Project documentation or configuration for the chosen mechanism
Complete discovery/resolution/access chain and proof the connection used that mechanism rather than cached IP/FQDN fallback
Endpoint IP/hostname, certificate, BMC firmware/serial identity and interface-MAC correlation with ambiguity/cache/proxy controls
After scope resolution: bounded invalid login, per-approved-role authenticated identity/access, logout and failed old-session reuse plus audit/lockout evidence
Explicit uncovered title/body coverage, cleanup/recovery and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items uniquely says `Login with MAC`, but Procedure and Criteria contain no MAC value, discovery/resolution step, URL form or MAC-specific expected result; they are a generic login/logout matrix nearly identical to the following Domain Name case. The title-specific target and method therefore cannot be tied to the body.

blocked_analysis.analysis: This is not blocked merely by a missing MAC value or package. The core meaning of MAC in a web-login operation and the evidence that distinguishes it from ordinary IP/FQDN login are absent. Selecting a MAC-derived hostname, discovery protocol or other mechanism would invent purpose and coverage, so engineer alignment is required before safe review-to-execution handoff.

review_improvement: Prevents a made-up MAC-to-URL convention or an ordinary web login from being reported as validation of an undefined MAC-specific access function and from exposing credentials to a wrong endpoint.
independent_technical_reasoning: A link-layer MAC identifies an interface within a network context; a web client needs a supported endpoint authority and transport route. Platforms may provide vendor discovery or MAC-derived naming, but those are distinct implementations that must be specified. Because the body never references any such mechanism and duplicates generic authentication steps, neither the operation nor the MAC-specific pass condition can be recovered safely from the source.
